thread:
acme-support: hey, hitting a weird failure in JSON mode after our model upgrade. Our schema validator throws "invalid string: does not match expected name form" for user names. Seems tied to Unicode normalization. Repro below.

acme-support: quick repro (streaming + structured):
```bash
curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.example/v1/respond" \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-structured-2026","stream":true,"structured":true,"input":"please return user as json {name, bio}"}'
```

acme-support: The streamed chunks reassemble to this final JSON that fails our server-side schema (expecting NFC precomposed chars):
```json
{"name":"Jose\u0301","bio":"Backend engineer\nLoves ☕"}
```

acme-support: Note: "Jose\u0301" is J-o-s-e + COMBINING ACUTE (NFD). Our validator expects "Jos\u00e9" (precomposed U+00E9). The mismatch causes an exact-string check to fail. Also saw token counting differ which affected billing reconciliation.

jamal: thanks for the repro. can you confirm the model and api flags? any custom post-processing on your side?

acme-support: model rwd-structured-2026, no client-side normalization — we assumed JSON mode would emit stable, normalized strings. streaming=true seems to be in play.

maria-fernandez: curious edge case — runtime sometimes emits combining sequences for diacritics because of tokenizer detokenization behavior for some code paths (esp. when using byte-level merges). streaming boundaries can expose that.

maria-fernandez: quick ask: can you paste the raw bytes from the response (hex or \u escapes)? that helps decide if it's NFD from the model or an escaping quirk during chunk joining.

acme-support: pasted raw escape output above (Jose\u0301). here's a fuller example from our capture showing chunk boundary:
```
chunk1: ...\"name\":\"Jos\u00
chunk2: 30 31\",\"bio\":\"Backend ...\"
```

taylor: that chunk split looks like \u escape was split across boundary: "Jos\u00\n 30 31" -> results in \u0301 after reassembly, but if any client join logic mangles it you can end up with different normalizations.

evan: filed SUP-4582 and assigned to eng-runtime. we should handle two things: 1) avoid splitting \u escapes across streaming chunks when emitting structured JSON, 2) normalize to NFC before finalizing structured output.

maria-fernandez: immediate workaround for customers: normalize on the client before validating, e.g. in Node: `const s = jsonStr.normalize('NFC')` then parse. For quick server-side mitigation we're going to roll a small post-process that NFC-normalizes structured outputs before escaping.

maria-fernandez: patch rolling to prod in ~20m that will:
- join streaming buffer with awareness of split \\u escapes
- run String.prototype.normalize('NFC') on every JSON string value before final JSON escaping

support-bot: deploy SUP-4582/patch-2026.03.17 started — estimated 20m to full rollout. /deploy logs: https://deploys.redwood/4582

acme-support: thanks — any ETA on whether this will also address token-count differences that hit billing? we saw a 4% delta on a daily report (higher token count when combining sequences were present).

maria-fernandez: normalizing to NFC reduces variability in tokenization for downstream counters; we expect the billing drift to shrink. we'll follow up once metrics post-rollout stabilize.

acme-support: confirmed: after your patch our ingestion and schema checks passed for the previous failing payload. tokens look more consistent too. :white_check_mark:

jamal: closing the thread here but leaving SUP-4582 open until metrics look stable across 24h. thanks everyone for quick triage.

acme-support: much appreciated — please keep us posted if you need further logs.
